title: Probe-driven SLO matrix and phased rollback playbook for hosted inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a pragmatic SLO matrix for hosted inference endpoints that is driven by active probes (synthetic transactions) and production telemetry, and establish a phased rollback and canary gating playbook for model and runtime deploys. This ticket consolidates acceptance criteria, probe definitions, burn-rate thresholds, probe-to-production reconciliation steps, and an automated gating policy for canary traffic and progressive rollout.

Background: We have recurring incidents where tail latency regressions or cache-invalidations only surface after ~30–60 minutes of traffic. Engineers need deterministic, probeable signals that map to error-budgets and can automatically block rollouts or trigger staged rollback. The goal is to reduce mean time to detect regressions on new model/runtime combos, provide clear handoffs for on-call, and create CI/CD gating that prevents noisy regressions from reaching full production.

Scope: Hosted API endpoints (text-generation and streaming chat) only. Does not cover Dedicated or Private deployments (follow-up ticket recommended). Includes probe definition, dashboard queries, alert thresholds, canary traffic weighting plan, manual rollback runbook, and CI contract tests.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic probe suite (cold-start + steady-state + tail-load) is defined with exact input templates and expected token-length distributions
SLO matrix created: p50/p95/p99 latency bands, 99.9% success rate, and per-minute request availability; each row has explicit error budget and burn rate thresholds
Automated canary gating flow implemented in CI to block promotion when probe burn-rate > 2x baseline for 10m or when p99 increases > 30% vs baseline for 5m
Dashboard panels and alert rules created in Ops Grafana for probe-vs-production divergence and a single-pane on-call runbook link
Rollback playbook documented: fast rollback (<5m) for severe burn, staged rollback (reduce to 10% traffic -> 0%) for moderate burn, and escalation steps defined for false-positives
Run CI contract tests that exercise quantized model variant and fallback routing; passing tests required before canary 25% ramp
rollout_gates: Gate 0 - CI contract: unit + model-compat tests green (no regressions)
Gate 1 - Canary 1 (1% traffic, 30m): block if probe_burn_rate_5m >= 4x baseline or probe_p99 >= 2x baseline
Gate 2 - Canary 2 (10% traffic, 60m): block if probe_burn_rate_10m >= 2x baseline or production_p99 delta > 30% and customer-impacting errors observed
Gate 3 - Progressive ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 hours): abort on sustained burn_rate > 1.5x baseline for 30m or kv_cache_miss_rate increase > 5 percentage points
Emergency fast-fail: immediate traffic cut to fallback model when error_rate_production_1m > 0.5% or availability < 99% for 5m
notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive probe sensitivity reduces time-to-detect but increases false positives; chosen thresholds bias toward safety for high-customer-impact endpoints
Decision: Start with conservative canary windows (30–60m) and shorten based on historical signal quality after two successful rollouts
Future: Add tenant-weighted SLOs and per-tenant canary lanes in a follow-up ticket
On-call handoff: first responder will validate probe inputs against live traffic repros before initiating rollback
